question: What are the genetic changes related to X-linked hyper IgM syndrome ?
reference_answers: Mutations in the CD40LG gene leading to an abnormal CD40 ligand or preventing its production.
generated_answer: Mutations in the MAF gene that disrupt the production or assembly of IgM molecules.
high_temp_samples: Mutations in the DDX3X gene that disrupt the production of antibodies.
A disorder of the immune system in which IgM antibodies are abnormally produced.
Mutations in the CD161 gene, which is a receptor for IgM antibodies.
Mutations in the B4GALT1 gene that disrupt the production or assembly of type XI collagen molecules.
Mutations in the CARD9 gene, which results in increased production of IgM antibodies.
Mutations in the IGHMBP2 gene that disrupt the production or assembly of type-I collagen molecules.
Mutations in the MHC class I gene that disrupt the production or assembly of MHC class I molecules.
A rare disorder characterized by a lack of immunoglobulin M (IgM), the main antibody component of the immune system.
Mutations in the FANCC gene that disrupt the production or assembly of immunoglobulin M molecules.
Mutations in the CD163 gene that disrupt the production of the IgM antibody molecules.
